## Historical audit — S0138

**Scope:** Only chunk 2 of 2 is visible; the reference and rendered images themselves are not available for independent inspection. All citations below refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C2/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal and scene | The student was instructed to reconstruct a single indoor RGB photograph in Blender, matching camera, framing, occlusion and materials using separate meshes. Its inferred scene interpretation was a chaise interior with wall, floor, curtains, pillow, label and cropped cane chair. The photograph is not visible here, so these identifications are not independently verified. [line 19, `model_request`, characters 0–185141] |
| Construction | The visible programs define multiple assemblies and separate chaise apron, legs, filled wings, head and cushion; they also define procedural striped fabric, parquet and cane materials. Parenting and coordinates express intended part relationships, but do not establish actual contact, absence of intersections or correct pose. [line 19, `model_request`, characters 0–185141] |
| Exploration and changes | After step 1, the student estimated horizontal compression and wall-slope error, changed camera position and lens, rotated the pillow, and altered fabric and floor settings. After step 2, it estimated a misplaced wall base and changed wall distance and angle, also moving the foreground chair. These are student diagnoses and executed program changes, not verified image improvements. [line 19, `model_request`, characters 0–185141] |
| Validation and outcome | Feedback embedded in the request reports successful renders for steps 1 and 2; step 3 independently has `execution_result` `ok: true`, a finished 16-sample render and saved PNG and blend file. The student then selected step 3. This is **technical execution and selection success; visual correctness and formal task success remain unknown**, not an empty patch or visible technical interruption. [line 17, `execution_result`, characters 0–40644; line 19, `model_request`, characters 0–185141; line 21, `model_response`, characters 0–350; line 22, `select`, characters 0–59] |
| Input and autonomy | The actual visible input includes system procedure and repeated runner feedback requesting landmark-based comparisons and narrow revisions; the student’s comments and revisions show use of that procedure. No separate teacher detection, diagnosis or proposed update is visible in this chunk, so separate teacher receipt or adoption cannot be established. The final student session had no tool calls and was restricted to selection; earlier revision programs demonstrate student-led exploration within the supplied workflow. [line 19, `model_request`, characters 0–185141; line 20, `codex_session`, characters 0–4315] |

**Transferable lesson:** A successful render confirms execution, not image fidelity; landmark comparisons, component structure and material settings require visual or geometric checks. **Task-specific unresolved hypotheses:** whether moving and rotating the wall corrected its apparent slope, whether the chair is correctly cropped, and whether upholstery, supports, pillow pose, lighting and floor tones match the photograph. The student’s claimed matches and object names are not independent verification.
